absent: Complete structure layouts for keepers, trackers, clocksources, timers, events, and control blocks beyond the fields observed in use.
Behavior of NTP helpers, clock reading, shadow publication, coarse refresh, second overflow handling, and displacement updates not routed here.
Calling contexts, interrupt handling, and serialization for advance, adjustment, accumulation, and offset changes.
Contents of the POSIX clock table, dynamic and processor clock operations, and namespace correction semantics.
Signal queue management, reference lifetime, hash lookup, resource accounting, and privilege evaluation internals.
Selection between tick and frequency advance modes, suspend and resume handling, and boot ordering.
Numeric values of resolution constants, tick limits, frequency scaling, and identifier ranges.

findings.text: The keeper maintains a seconds valued TAI displacement together with a base real displacement. Updating the TAI offset stores the new seconds value and recomputes the derived TAI displacement as the sum of the real displacement and the new offset expressed as whole seconds. Leap corrections decrement the stored offset while shifting the wall to monotonic displacement in the opposite direction, preserving continuity of monotonic time.

Advancement is skipped while suspended. Otherwise the lane measures elapsed cycles since the last mono sample bounded by the maximum raw delta, returns early in tick mode when below one cycle interval, otherwise consumes elapsed cycles in successively smaller power of two multiples of the interval bounded to avoid tick length overflow, then corrects the rate, folds fractional nanoseconds into seconds, refreshes coarse nanoseconds only when progress occurred, publishes shadow state to the live keeper, and reports whether a clock set occurred.

Rate correction caches the current NTP tick length and skew delta. When either changes it recomputes the base multiplier from their sum scaled by the error shift and normalized by the cycle interval, after expanding the stored per HZ skew to a full rate. Otherwise it restores the base rate by removing the prior single step dither. A positive accumulated error then adds one to the multiplier, and the resulting delta is applied through a continuity preserving adjustment.

Frequency changes preserve the reported time for the current unaccumulated remainder. The multiplier moves by the requested delta, the per interval nanosecond increment moves by the same delta scaled by the cycle interval, the fractional nanosecond accumulator moves opposite to the remainder scaled likewise, and the NTP error accumulator moves with the remainder scaled by the error shift. Positive deltas that would wrap the mono multiplier are rejected with a one time warning.

Fractional mono time in shifted units is repeatedly folded into whole seconds using the shifted seconds constant. A borrow flag from a prior underflow suppresses one NTP second notification. Otherwise each new second invokes the leap handler, and a nonzero leap shifts wall seconds, moves wall to monotonic displacement by the negated leap duration, decrements the TAI offset by the leap, and marks the clock as set.

Consumption of one shifted interval advances both mono and raw last cycle markers, adds the shifted mono interval to mono fractional time with second folding, adds the shifted raw interval to raw fractional time with independent raw second folding, and updates the NTP error by the shifted tick length minus the shifted interval scaled by the error shift, plus any drained skew contribution scaled to full rate when skewing is active. Smaller remainders leave state unchanged.

Adjtime control validation requires single shot offset mode to accompany the older adjtime mode, requires privilege for any modification or offset injection unless read only single shot, constrains tick to plus or minus ten percent around one million over user HZ, requires nonnegative subsecond offset below one second in nano or micro units according to mode, and rejects frequency values that would overflow scaled arithmetic on wide longs.

Auxiliary clocks reject leap insertion or deletion status, reject TAI offset setting, and reject pulse per second frequency or time status, reflecting that they behave like TAI without leaps or pulse support.

Raw and coarse readers provide sequence protected snapshots. Raw reads combine raw seconds with live raw nanoseconds. Coarse real reads return coarse wall seconds plus coarse nanoseconds. Coarse monotonic reads add the wall to monotonic displacement to the coarse wall value with normalization. A helper composes the coarse wall value from wall seconds and cached coarse nanoseconds.

POSIX clock callbacks map each clock flavor to its underlying accessor. Monotonic and raw variants return mono or raw time with namespace monotonic adjustment, realtime coarse returns coarse real time, monotonic coarse returns coarse mono with namespace adjustment, boottime variants return boottime with namespace boottime adjustment, TAI variants return TAI time, coarse resolution returns a low resolution constant, and hrtimer resolution returns the configured hrtimer granularity with zero seconds.

Timekeeper readers sample under a sequence counter with begin and retry pairing in a loop, re reading seconds, offsets, and displacements until a consistent snapshot is observed, allowing concurrent reads during updates from the advance path.

Signal delivery for POSIX timers serializes timer state with the per timer spinlock, while the outer delivery path releases the signal handler spinlock before acquiring the timer lock and reacquires it afterwards with interrupts still disabled, preserving a defined order between the two locks. The hrtimer expiry callback acquires the timer lock with interrupt state saved before queueing the signal.

Timer creation initializes the per timer lock before hashing, protects hash insertion and removal with the owning bucket lock under read copy update semantics, and publishes the timer to the owning signal list only while holding both the timer lock with interrupts disabled and the signal handler lock, so observers of a valid signal pointer see a fully initialized object.

A periodic timer awaiting requeue validates that signal and queue sequence numbers still match and that the timer remains valid, otherwise it drops without rearming. One shot timers report success without rearming. Periodic timers forward the hrtimer by the interval and attempt a user mode absolute restart, then transfer the accumulated overrun to the last overrun field, reset the running overrun to negative one, advance the signal sequence, publish a saturated overrun count into the signal info, and either remain armed or requeue a signal when restart fails.

Creation resolves the clock identifier to its operations, optionally fetches a requested identifier for restore when the owning process enabled that mode, allocates and hashes a timer with a fresh identifier in invalid state, validates any supplied event for target and signal number, defaults to alarm signal directed at the caller thread group when no event is given, copies the identifier to user space, invokes the clock specific creation hook, then clears the validity tag on the stored signal pointer and links the timer into the owner signal list. Failures unwind through unhash and release.

Rate paths guard against excessive skew by warning once when the adjusted mono multiplier deviates from the clock base multiplier by more than the clock allowed maximum, reject multiplier wrap with a one time warning, and repair negative fractional mono time after adjustment by borrowing one second and setting a flag that suppresses the next second overflow notification.

Control paths fail closed on invalid inputs and saturated arithmetic. Frequency scaling is rejected when outside the scaled range on wide longs, tick and offset ranges are enforced, timer overrun counts beyond signed 32 bit maximum are reported as saturated maximum, and mismatched signal sequences or invalid timers cause delivery to drop the signal rather than rearm.

Externally visible routines provided by these fragments are the raw and coarse kernel time getters, the POSIX timer signal delivery entry, the timer release helper, and the restore identifier control for timer creation. Internal helpers for accumulation, adjustment, validation, event checking, allocation, hashing, and clock lookup remain file local.

Observed keeper state includes an identifier, wall seconds, cached coarse nanoseconds, wall to monotonic displacement, raw seconds, TAI offset with real and TAI displacements, cycle interval with mono and raw per interval increments, NTP tick cache with skew delta and error accumulators plus error shift and single step dither, a second overflow skip flag, and mono and raw trackers each with last cycle marker with mask and clock limits plus multiplier with shift and fractional nanoseconds.

Observed POSIX timer state includes a numeric identifier with clock identifier and clock operations pointer, a spinlock, an hrtimer node with interval, signal and queue sequence numbers with status, running and last overrun counters, target process reference with type and notification mode, queued signal info with number value timer identifier and code, hash linkage with owner list linkage, reference counting with deferred release linkage, and a resource count handle for pending signals.

Validation recognizes mode identifiers ADJ_ADJTIME with ADJ_OFFSET_SINGLESHOT and ADJ_OFFSET_READONLY, plus ADJ_TICK ADJ_SETOFFSET ADJ_NANO ADJ_FREQUENCY ADJ_STATUS and ADJ_TAI, status flags STA_INS STA_DEL STA_PPSFREQ and STA_PPSTIME, capability CAP_SYS_TIME, time units NSEC_PER_SEC USEC_PER_SEC and USER_HZ, scaling PPM_SCALE with LLONG_MIN LLONG_MAX and BITS_PER_LONG, and error codes EINVAL EPERM and EFAULT as observed outcomes.

Timer creation and delivery use restore controls PR_TIMER_CREATE_RESTORE_IDS_OFF with ON and GET forms, notification selectors SIGEV_SIGNAL SIGEV_THREAD SIGEV_NONE and SIGEV_THREAD_ID, signal bounds SIGALRM and SIGRTMAX with code SI_TIMER, identifier markers TIMER_ANY_ID and INT_MAX, clock selectors CLOCKFD_MASK and CLOCKFD with dynamic and cpu clock fallbacks, resolution sources KTIME_LOW_RES and hrtimer_resolution, and status markers POSIX_TIMER_REQUEUE_PENDING and POSIX_TIMER_ARMED with overrun base negative one.
